# 2017 CS1 Q34: String not generated by S -> SaS | aSb | bSa | SS | epsilon

## Question

If $G$ is a grammar with productions

$$S \to SaS \mid aSb \mid bSa \mid SS \mid \epsilon$$

where $S$ is the start variable, then which one of the following strings is not generated by $G$?

- (A) $abab$
- (B) $aaab$
- (C) $abbaa$
- (D) $babba$

<details class="success" markdown="1">
<summary>Answer</summary>

**D**

</details>

<details class="info" markdown="1">
<summary>Solution</summary>

**Find an invariant.** Let $d = \#a - \#b$ of a string.

| Production | Effect on $d$ |
|---|---|
| $S \to \epsilon$ | $d = 0$ |
| $S \to aSb$, $S \to bSa$ | adds one $a$ and one $b$, so $d$ unchanged |
| $S \to SS$ | $d$ adds up |
| $S \to SaS$ | adds one extra $a$, so $d$ goes up by $1$ |

So every string of $L(G)$ has $\#a \ge \#b$. A string with more $b$'s than $a$'s cannot be generated.

**Check the options.**

| String | $(\#a, \#b)$ | Generated? |
|---|---|---|
| (A) $abab$ | $(2,2)$ | Yes: $S\to SS$, each $S \to aSb$ with $S\to\epsilon$ |
| (B) $aaab$ | $(3,1)$ | Yes: $S \to aSb$ with inner $S \Rightarrow aa$ (via $SS$, each $SaS$ giving $a$) |
| (C) $abbaa$ | $(3,2)$ | Yes: $S \to SaS$ with first $S \Rightarrow abba$ (via $SS$: $aSb$ gives $ab$, $bSa$ gives $ba$), the middle $a$, and last $S\to\epsilon$ |
| (D) $babba$ | $(2,3)$ | **No**: $\#b > \#a$ |

So the string not generated is **(D)**.

**Code check:** generating the language up to length 7 as a fixed point, (A), (B), (C) were all generated and (D) was not. Every generated string had $\#a \ge \#b$, and every string up to length 7 with $\#a\ge\#b$ was generated.

**Key idea:** look for an invariant of the grammar. Here no production can add a $b$ without also adding an $a$.

</details>
